reset_app_state.source:
async def reset_app_state(state: "BaseState") -> None:
    """Reset only the authed surface of each non-exempt state (called on logout).

    A user's session data must not survive into the next user logging in on the
    same client token, but state the developer opted public via
    ``rxe.field(auth=False)`` / ``rxe.var(auth=False)`` is not part of the
    authenticated session and is preserved. Per non-exempt state this resets the
    protected (``auth`` is not ``False``) base vars and drops the protected
    computed-var caches, and always resets server-only backend vars (they never
    reach the client and have no ``auth=False`` opt-out).

    Exempt framework/provider states are skipped — their tokens are cleared
    separately by ``_reset_auth``. The protection map holds exactly the
    non-exempt states (the sweep registers every tree node), so resetting each
    entry in place covers the whole app without recursion.

    Args:
        state: Any state instance off the current event's state tree.

    Raises:
        Exception: A state failed to reset, after the remaining states have
            also been attempted.
    """
    first_reset_error: Exception | None = None
    for state_cls, overrides in _PROTECTION.items():
        try:
            substate = await state.get_state(state_cls)
        except Exception:
            continue  # fail closed: an unloadable state just stays as-is
        try:
            _reset_protected(substate, overrides)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.exception(
                "Failed to reset protected state %s", state_cls.get_full_name()
            )
            if first_reset_error is None:
                first_reset_error = exc
    # Finish clearing other states, but do not silently report a successful reset.
    if first_reset_error is not None:
        raise first_reset_error

_reset_protected.source:
def _reset_protected(substate: "BaseState", overrides: dict[str, AuthValue]) -> None:
    """Reset one state's protected base vars + backend vars to their defaults.

    Args:
        substate: The state instance to reset in place.
        overrides: The recorded protection entry for the state's class.
    """
    state_cls = type(substate)
    fields = state_cls.get_fields()
    # Protected base vars revert to their declared defaults; public (auth=False)
    # fields survive the logout.
    for name in state_cls.base_vars:
        if _auth_for(state_cls, overrides, name) is False:
            continue
        setattr(substate, name, _field_default(fields[name]))
    # Backend vars never reach the client and have no auth=False opt-out, so
    # always clear them. Inherited ones are reset on the state that owns them.
    for name in get_backend_var_names(state_cls, own_only=True):
        value = (
            copy.deepcopy(get_backend_var_default(state_cls, name))
            if _HAS_BACKEND_VARS
            else _field_default(fields[name])
        )
        setattr(substate, name, value)
    # Drop every protected cached computed var: setting a base var only
    # invalidates computed vars through the dependency graph, so a cached one with
    # no tracked dependency on a reset var keeps a stale value that would leak to
    # the next user on this client token. Then, for the ones that HAVE an anonymous
    # placeholder, also mark them dirty so this client's post-logout delta
    # re-delivers them and the filter swaps in the placeholder -- blanking the
    # authed value rather than leaving it rendered until a rehydrate. A protected
    # computed var WITHOUT a placeholder (no ``initial_value``) is dropped by the
    # filter regardless, so forcing it into the delta would only recompute the
    # getter to discard the result -- wasted work, and a getter that cannot run
    # against the reset state would needlessly break the logout delta; it is left
    # to recompute lazily on next access. Public (auth=False) caches are untouched.
    dirtied_computed = False
    for name, cvar in state_cls.computed_vars.items():
        if _auth_for(state_cls, overrides, name) is False:
            continue
        cvar.mark_dirty(instance=substate)
        if _anon_placeholder(state_cls, name) is not _NO_PLACEHOLDER:
            substate.dirty_vars.add(name)
            dirtied_computed = True
    # A substate whose only resets are computed vars (no base/backend vars set
    # above) was never marked dirty via ``setattr``; propagate so its delta is
    # included. ``_mark_dirty`` is a no-op for propagation on a standalone inst.
    if dirtied_computed:
        substate._mark_dirty()

_reset_session.source:
async def _reset_session(self):
        """Clear this provider's tokens and reset non-exempt app state.

        The single deauthentication chokepoint: every logout / expiry / token
        failure path funnels here so a user's app state never outlives their
        tokens. Without it, the per-client state (and cached computed vars)
        would survive a logout and leak to the next user logging in on the same
        client token (the Reflex client token outlives the OIDC session).
        """
        self._reset_auth()
        await self._reset_plugin_owned_state()

_reset_plugin_owned_state.source:
async def _reset_plugin_owned_state(self) -> None:
        """Reset the deauthentication state the ``AuthPlugin`` owns.

        The half of ``_reset_session`` that reaches outside this provider: the
        app-state sweep and ``AuthUserState`` both belong to the plugin, while
        clearing this provider's own cookies does not. Split out so the
        plugin-presence guard sits on a definition of its own — the provider
        still clears its cookies in an app with no ``AuthPlugin``.
        """
        from reflex_enterprise.auth.enforcement import reset_app_state
        from reflex_enterprise.auth.user_state import AuthUserState

        await reset_app_state(self)
        auth_user = await self.get_state(AuthUserState)
        auth_user.reset()
